<task_result>
Now I have a comprehensive picture. Here is a complete summary of all findings.

---

## Search Results: Keyboard Scroll Behavior with 'j'/'k' Key Bindings

I found **6 files** implementing keyboard scroll behavior with vim-style 'j'/'k' key bindings. Here is each file with its role and relevant implementation details.

---

### 1. `/Users/samforeman/projects/saforem2/sam.onl/web/src/utils/vim.ts` (Core utility - 353 lines)

This is the **central utility module** that provides reusable vim-navigation primitives used across the site.

**Key exports:**
- `isUserTyping()` (line 2) -- guard to skip key handlers when user is in an input/textarea/contenteditable
- `applyVimCursorHighlight()` (line 72) -- applies a blinking CSS `::highlight(vim)` pseudo-class to the first character of the focused element
- `vimFocusElement()` (line 108) -- focuses an element, scrolls it into view (temporarily disabling scroll-snap to avoid fights), and applies the vim cursor highlight
- `applyVimNavigation()` (line 133) -- the main function: attaches a `keydown` listener to a container element that implements `j`/`k`/`ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` (next/prev), `g`/`G` (first/last), and `zz` (center-scroll) navigation across all elements matching a query selector
- `paginateElements()` (line 342) -- helper returning `{first, next, prev, last}` relative to a given element in a list

**Core j/k logic (lines 239-339):**
- Line 280: `const isNextKey = e.key === 'j' || e.key === 'ArrowDown'`
- Line 281: `const isPrevKey = e.key === 'k' || e.key === 'ArrowUp'`
- Lines 294-313: When no element is currently focused (`activeIndex === -1`), it finds the first element visible in the viewport and focuses from there
- Lines 316-328: When an element IS focused, `j` moves to `activeIndex + 1`, `k` moves to `activeIndex - 1`
- Lines 182-214: `focusFromIndex` temporarily disables `scroll-snap-type` on the nearest `<main>`, calls `.focus()` + `.scrollIntoView()`, then re-enables snap in a `requestAnimationFrame`

---

### 2. `/Users/samforeman/projects/saforem2/sam.onl/web/src/utils/scroll.ts` (Scroll snap utility - 50 lines)

A supporting utility for **scroll-snap change detection**. Not directly related to j/k keys, but used by components that work alongside vim navigation.

- `determineSnapTarget()` (line 3) -- finds the snap target currently visible in the viewport
- `attachScrollSnapListener()` (line 25) -- cross-browser scroll-snap listener (Chromium `scrollsnapchange`, Firefox `scrollend`, Safari `scroll` fallback)

---

### 3. `/Users/samforeman/projects/saforem2/sam.onl/web/src/components/landing/VimNavigation.astro` (UI component - 159 lines)

This is the **visible vim navigation bar** (h/j/k/l/slash buttons) displayed on the landing page.

**Key behavior (lines 48-158):**
- Line 68: Calls `applyVimNavigation(content, vimQuery)` on `<main>` to enable j/k cycling through focusable links/buttons
- Lines 74-116: **Bootstrap handler** -- when j/k is pressed and focus is *outside* `<main>`, it finds the first visible tabbable element inside `<main>` and focuses it, so the container-scoped `applyVimNavigation` can take over
- Lines 129-141: **Visual feedback** -- on `keydown`, highlights the corresponding button (j/k/h/l) by changing its `variant-` attribute to `foreground1`
- Lines 144-158: **Reset feedback** -- on `keyup`, resets the button variant back to `background2`

---

### 4. `/Users/samforeman/projects/saforem2/sam.onl/web/src/layouts/Doc.astro` (Doc layout - 1081 lines)

The **document/page layout** with the most extensive vim keyboard handling. Multiple layers of j/k behavior:

**Layer 1: Navbar/Main crossover (lines 324-415)**
- Lines 324-328: `isPlainPrevKey` -- detects `k` or `ArrowUp` (unmodified)
- Lines 330-334: `isPlainNextKey` -- detects `j` or `ArrowDown` (unmodified)
- Lines 364-387: Captures `k` on `mainContent` -- when focus is on the *first* main element and `k` is pressed, focus jumps to the navbar (cross-region navigation)
- Lines 389-415: Captures `j` on `navbar` -- when focus is on the *last* navbar element and `j` is pressed, focus jumps into main content

**Layer 2: Bootstrap focus from unfocused state (lines 417-457)**
- Lines 443-448: `j`/`ArrowDown` with nothing focused -- focuses the first visible main element
- Lines 450-456: `k`/`ArrowUp` with nothing focused -- focuses the last visible main element

**Layer 3: Shift+h/j/k/l region jumping (lines 471-508)**
- Line 476: Detects `Shift` + any of `h`, `j`, `k`, `l`
- Line 486: `Shift+J` -- jump focus to the first visible main content element
- Line 494: `Shift+K` -- jump focus to the navbar

**Layer 4: `z` chord navigation (lines 797-927)**
- Lines 863-870: `z` then `j` -- focus the main content area
- Lines 873-880: `z` then `k` -- focus the navbar

**Layer 5: Ctrl+j/k region focus (lines 887-925)**
- Lines 909-916: `Ctrl+J` -- focus the main content area
- Lines 918-925: `Ctrl+K` -- focus the navbar

**Also: `h`/`l` plain key handling (lines 510-549)** for sidebar/TOC navigation.

---

### 5. `/Users/samforeman/projects/saforem2/sam.onl/web/src/components/Filter.astro` (lines 495-563)

Implements j/k navigation within **dialog/modal contexts**:

- Lines 544-548: In the **theme dialog**, `j`/`ArrowDown` cycles to the next theme button (wrapping)
- Lines 551-556: `k`/`ArrowUp` cycles to the previous theme button (wrapping)
- Lines 667-685: In the **search dialog input**, `Ctrl+N`/`ArrowDown` and `Ctrl+P`/`ArrowUp` navigate search results (does NOT use j/k here since the user is typing in the search input)

---

### 6. `/Users/samforeman/projects/saforem2/sam.onl/web/src/components/ui/Dropdown.astro` (lines 106-114)

A **custom dropdown element** (`<select-dropdown>`) with vim keys:

- Line 112: `e.key === 'ArrowDown' || e.key === 'j'` -- focus next item
- Line 113: `e.key === 'ArrowUp' || e.key === 'k'` -- focus previous item

---

### Summary of the Architecture

The implementation follows a layered design:

| Layer | File | Scope | Purpose |
|-------|------|-------|---------|
| **Core utility** | `vim.ts` | Reusable | `applyVimNavigation()` -- attaches j/k/g/G/zz to any container+query |
| **Scroll utility** | `scroll.ts` | Reusable | Cross-browser scroll-snap detection (supports vim.ts's snap-disable strategy) |
| **Landing page** | `VimNavigation.astro` | Landing page | Visual j/k/h/l buttons + bootstrap handler to seed focus into `<main>` |
| **Doc layout** | `Doc.astro` | All doc pages | Multi-region vim navigation (navbar, sidebar, main, TOC) with plain/Shift/Ctrl/z-chord modifiers |
| **Filter/dialogs** | `Filter.astro` | Dialogs | j/k inside theme picker dialog |
| **Dropdown** | `Dropdown.astro` | Custom element | j/k inside dropdown menus |

The scroll behavior works by calling `element.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })` after `.focus()`, with a key pattern of temporarily setting `scrollSnapType = 'none'` on the scroll container and restoring it in `requestAnimationFrame` to prevent mandatory scroll-snap from fighting the programmatic scroll.

parts.text:
**The fix:** In `web/src/utils/vim.ts:306`, the `k` key handler when no element was focused (`activeIndex === -1`) was using direction `1` (forward) — identical to the `j` handler. This meant pressing `k` moved focus forward instead of backward, making it behave the same as `j`.

Changed the direction from `1` to `-1` so `k` correctly navigates **backward** through the focusable elements, starting from the first visible viewport element and scanning upward.

This is consistent with how `Doc.astro` handles the unfocused case (lines 450-456), where `k` focuses the **last** visible element while `j` focuses the **first**.

The build passes cleanly.

parts.text:
Yes, that's the bug. The `focus` event bubbles. When `focusFromIndex` calls `a.focus()`:

1. The `<a>` gets focus
2. The `focus` event fires on `<a>`, triggering `a.onfocus` -> `vimFocusElement(a)` -> `a.focus()` (redundant but OK)
3. The `focus` event **bubbles** up to `<li>` 
4. `<li>` has `onfocus` assigned too -> `vimFocusElement(li)` -> `li.focus()`
5. Focus moves BACK to `<li>`, stealing it from `<a>`
6. `focusFromIndex` checks `document.activeElement === a` -> **false** (it's now the `<li>`)
7. The `<a>` is skipped, and the loop moves to the next `<li>`

The fix: use `addEventListener('focus', ..., { once: true })` won't help since it's reassigned each time. The real fix is to guard the `onfocus` handler so it only fires when the element itself received focus, not when a child did. The `onfocus` handler should check that the event target is the element itself. But since `onfocus` is a property (not addEventListener), we don't get the event object.

The simplest fix: switch from `el.onfocus` to `el.addEventListener('focus', ...)` and check `e.target === el` to ignore bubbled focus events.

parts.text:
There's the problem. The landing page has **two** vim navigation systems both applied to `<main>`:

1. `Doc.astro` applies `applyVimNavigation(mainContent, '[tabindex="0"], a[href], summary')` — includes headings/paragraphs with `tabindex="0"`
2. `VimNavigation.astro` applies `applyVimNavigation(content, 'a[href], button:not(#btn-j)...')` — only matches `a[href]` and `button`, **no** `[tabindex="0"]`

Both attach keydown listeners to `<main>`. And the VimNavigation bootstrap (line 74-116) finds the first visible `a[href]` or `button` — which would be the first link inside the "About" paragraph, skipping the `<h2>` entirely.

The VimNavigation bootstrap handler fires on the `window` and calls `vimFocusElement(target)` on the first link. Meanwhile the Doc.astro bootstrap also fires on `window`. The order depends on which script loads first. Since VimNavigation.astro is loaded as a separate module, it may race with Doc.astro.

But more fundamentally: the VimNavigation component's query (`vimQuery`) doesn't include `[tabindex="0"]`, so it only navigates links and buttons — not headings, paragraphs, or list items.

The fix: VimNavigation should use the same query that includes `[tabindex="0"]` elements, or better yet, the landing page shouldn't have two competing vim navigation systems. Let me check if VimNavigation is only used on the landing page:

## Summary of all fixes

### 1. `web/src/utils/vim.ts:306` — `k` direction when unfocused
Pressing `k` with nothing focused was going forward (direction `1`) instead of backward (direction `-1`). Fixed to `-1`.

### 2. `web/src/layouts/Doc.astro:336` — `applyMainContentTabIndex` 
Two changes:
- Removed the `focusableChildQuery` skip logic so ALL direct children of `#main-content` and ALL `<li>` elements get `tabindex="0"` — making headings, paragraphs, list items, and divs all navigable via `j`/`k`.
- Added a skip for `<ul>`/`<ol>` containers (navigated via their `<li>` children) to avoid a parent-child focus trap.

### 3. `web/src/utils/vim.ts:173` — `onfocus` event bubbling
The `onfocus` handler was firing when a child received focus (because `focus` bubbles). When focusing an `<a>` inside a `<li>`, the event would bubble to the `<li>`, whose handler would call `li.focus()`, stealing focus back. Added `e.target !== el` guard to only handle direct focus events.

### 4. `web/src/components/landing/VimNavigation.astro:57` — Missing `[tabindex="0"]` in query
The VimNavigation component's query only matched `a[href]` and `button`, missing all the `[tabindex="0"]` elements (headings, paragraphs, list items, divs). This caused the competing vim handler to skip those elements. Added `[tabindex="0"]` to the query to match the same elements as Doc.astro.

## Goal Fix the `j`/`k` vim-style keyboard scroll/navigation behavior in the main content area of the site (an Astro-based personal website). The user wants `j`/`k` to navigate through **every** content element in document order — headings, paragraphs, divs, list items, AND the links/buttons inside them — not just links. The expected behavior is like a vim cursor moving through a document: `

` → `` (heading anchor) → `
` → `

` → `` (link in paragraph) → next `

  • ` → `` (link in li) → etc. ## Instructions - All content elements (headings, paragraphs, `
    ` blocks, `
  • ` items) should be focusable and navigable via `j`/`k` - When pressing `j` on a container element (like a `
    ` or `
  • `) that contains a link, the link should be the **next** focused element before moving to the next sibling - `
      `/`
        ` containers should NOT be focusable (to avoid focus traps), but their `

        ` block below, etc. ## Discoveries 1. **Architecture**: The vim navigation system has multiple layers: - `web/src/utils/vim.ts` — Core utility with `applyVimNavigation()` that attaches keydown handlers - `web/src/layouts/Doc.astro` — Doc layout that calls `applyVimNavigation(mainContent, queryString)` and assigns `tabindex="0"` to content elements via `applyMainContentTabIndex()` - `web/src/components/landing/VimNavigation.astro` — Visual j/k/h/l button bar that ALSO calls `applyVimNavigation(content, vimQuery)` on `
        ` 2. **Duplicate handlers problem**: On Doc.astro pages, BOTH Doc.astro AND VimNavigation.astro call `applyVimNavigation()` on `
        `, creating two competing keydown handlers with different query selectors. The VimNavigation script loads FIRST (line 1517 in rendered HTML) while Doc.astro loads later (line 2894). When both fire on the same keypress, one steals focus from the other. 3. **Focus event bubbling**: The `onfocus` handler in `vim.ts` was causing parent elements to steal focus back from children because the `focus` event bubbles. When an `` inside a `

      3. `, whose handler calls `li.focus()`, stealing focus back. 4. **`

I can see the critical `onfocus` guard is in place:

```js
i.onfocus = n => { n.target === i && (F(i), o?.(i)) }
```

The `n.target === i` check prevents the focus-stealing via event bubbling. When a child `<a>` inside a `<li>` gets focus, the event bubbles to the `<li>`, but because `n.target` is the `<a>` (not the `<li>`), the handler doesn't re-focus the `<li>`.

Also confirmed the `k` direction fix: when `w === -1` (unfocused), pressing `k` calls `l(n, d, -1)` (backward direction).

Now let me spot-check the actual HTML content for tabindex attributes on a Doc.astro page:

The tabindex is applied at runtime via the `H()` function (the `applyMainContentTabIndex` equivalent), not in the static HTML. That's expected — the function runs client-side on page load. Let me verify by checking what the `H()` function does in the minified code: it calls `t.setAttribute("tabindex","0")` on elements that don't already have it. This is correct — the static HTML won't have tabindex on `

`, `

`, `

` because those are added by the script at runtime.

All tasks are complete. Here's a summary:

## Status: All done

### Build
Build passes cleanly -- 106 pages built, 8/8 turbo tasks succeeded, zero errors.

### Verified in built output

1. **VimNavigation script** (`BDuETL4k.js`):
   - `vimQuery` includes `[tabindex="0"]`
   - `applyVimNavigation` is skipped when `main.id` exists (i.e., on Doc.astro pages where `id="main-content"`)
   - Bootstrap `window.addEventListener("keydown", ...)` is also skipped on Doc.astro pages via the same `isDocManaged` guard

2. **Doc.astro script** (`CJFL9npS.js`):
   - `applyMainContentTabIndex` correctly skips `<ul>`/`<ol>` containers, sets `tabindex="0"` on all other direct children of `#main-content`, and on all `<li>` elements
   - `mainItemQuery` = `'[tabindex="0"], a[href], summary'` -- matches all content elements
   - `applyVimNavigation` is called with the scoped query `#main-content [tabindex="0"], a[href], summary`

3. **vim.ts core** (`vim.MihZzemJ.js`):
   - `onfocus` handler has the `n.target === i` guard to prevent focus-stealing via event bubbling
   - `k` key when unfocused correctly navigates backward (`-1` direction)

4. **Sidebar.astro**: Calls `applyVimNavigation` on `#sidebar` (its own element), not on `<main>` -- no conflict with Doc.astro.

5. **Home page** (`index.html`): Uses `<main data-landing>` with no `id`, so VimNavigation correctly runs its own `applyVimNavigation` there.

### What you should test manually
Run `bun run dev` (or `bun run preview`) and verify:
- On a **Doc.astro page** (e.g., `/posts/2025/11/12/`): Press `j` to navigate through heading -> anchor link -> div -> paragraph -> link -> li -> link, etc.
- On the **landing page** (`/`): Press `j` to navigate through content elements
- Press `k` when nothing is focused -- it should start from the bottom of the viewport, not the top
